predictor.lessonTitle: Module 1: Your First Lines of Code
predictor.title: Print Output Sequencing
predictor.code:
print("Code", end="-")
print("Tutor", end=" ")
print("Africa")
predictor.explanation: The end parameter controls what is printed at the end of the line: end="-" connects Code and Tutor, end=" " adds space before Africa.

predictor.lessonTitle: Module 3: Data Types: Strings, Numbers, and Booleans
predictor.title: Type Casting & Arithmetic Evaluation
predictor.code:
x = "10"
y = 2
print(x * y)
predictor.explanation: Multiplying a string by an integer in Python repeats the string. "10" * 2 results in "1010".

predictor.title: Operator Precedence & Modulo
predictor.code:
a = 17
b = 5
print(a // b, a % b)
predictor.explanation: 17 // 5 gives floor integer division 3, while 17 % 5 gives remainder 2.

predictor.title: Truthy vs Falsy Comparisons
predictor.code: print(bool(""), bool("False"), bool(0))
predictor.explanation: Empty strings and 0 are falsy in Python. Non-empty strings like "False" evaluate to True!

predictor.title: Short-Circuit Logic Predictions
predictor.code:
a = True
b = False
print(a or b and not a)
predictor.explanation: Logical NOT and AND have higher precedence than OR. But because a is True, short-circuit evaluation immediately evaluates True.

predictor.title: Positional vs Keyword Precedence
predictor.explanation: Keyword arguments override the default parameter value for msg.

predictor.title: Implicit None Return Value
predictor.code:
def get_data():
    x = 10
result = get_data()
print(result)
predictor.explanation: Functions in Python without an explicit return statement implicitly return None.

predictor.title: In-Place vs Returning Sort
predictor.code:
nums = [1, 2, 3]
print([x * 2 for x in nums if x > 1])
predictor.explanation: List comprehension filters elements greater than 1 ([2, 3]) and multiplies each by 2 ([4, 6]).

predictor.title: KeyError vs .get() Fallback
predictor.explanation: .get("age", 25) returns the fallback value 25 without modifying the original dictionary, so "age" in user remains False.

predictor.title: Complex Comprehension & Filter
predictor.code:
nums = [1, 2, 3]
print([x * 2 for x in nums if x > 1])
predictor.explanation: List comprehension filters elements greater than 1 ([2, 3]) and multiplies each by 2 ([4, 6]).
